newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Davdyov says no gov't grain imports in 97.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Davdyov says no gov't grain imports in 97.

text.p: Russian Foreign Trade Minister Oleg Davydov said on Friday that the government would not import grain this year.

"Russia will not conduct centralised grain imports this year," said Davydov, repeating comments made in recent months by government and industry officials that any grain imports would be carried out by private companies.
Davydov, also a deputy prime minister, was speaking to correspondents in the Urals city of Yekaterinburg.

The government, once one of the world's biggest grain buyers, has left the international grain market, saying that it has no cash or credit for purchases and that private traders must make up for shortfalls.

Russia's private-sector grain imports have soared in recent years. Some of the buying is backed by credits and guarantees from regional administrations, but these are not considered centralised, or government-sponsored, grain imports.
